subject: Electrical Engineering
title: RMS: The Useful AC Value
description: A quick win: understand RMS: The Useful AC Value.

hook.text: A 120V outlet actually peaks at 170V. The 120V number is the RMS value.

buildup.text: AC swings from peak positive to peak negative. Its average is zero — useless.

discovery.text: RMS means root mean square — it equals the DC voltage that delivers the same power.

twist.text: RMS is always about 70.7% of the peak value for a sine wave.

climax.text: Every voltage rating on an appliance is RMS. It's the number that matters for power.

punchline.text: RMS tells you what AC actually delivers — not what it promises.

quiz.question: Why is RMS used instead of peak voltage?
options: Peak voltage is impossible to measure accurately
RMS equals the DC voltage that delivers the same heating power
RMS is always exactly half the peak value
